task: API cleanup: every other exponential wait class uses `multiplier`, but `wait_exponential_jitter` uses `initial`. Add a `multiplier` parameter (default 1) to `wait_exponential_jitter` with the same meaning, and deprecate `initial`: passing `initial` (by keyword or positionally) must still work but emit a `DeprecationWarning`, and passing both `initial` and `multiplier` must raise `ValueError`.
why:
The decider was fidelity: existing callers that read `wait_exponential_jitter(...).initial` must keep working. c1 removes the `self.initial` attribute without a replacement, so code reading `obj.initial` would now get an `AttributeError`. c2, c3 and c4 keep it as a read-only alias of `multiplier`.
c4 also edits `doc/source/index.rst`, adding a new documentation section and example that the task did not ask for.
c3 and c2 have the same implementation. I picked c3 for its tests: they set `jitter=0` so the expected values are exact, and they also cover passing `initial` positionally together with `multiplier=`, and that the warning points at the caller's file. c2 is a near-tie runner-up; it lost only on those tests.
